lines.say: The company is A B InBev, the owner of Anheuser-Busch. In twenty twenty-five it brought in fifty-nine point three billion dollars in revenue.

lines.text: Selling less and earning more is the whole trick, and by the end you'll know exactly how they pull it off.

lines.text: Chapter 1: An empire built on deals
lines.say: Chapter one: an empire built on deals.

lines.text: Anheuser-Busch, the St. Louis brewer behind Budweiser, was American for well over a century. Then came 2008.
lines.say: Anheuser-Busch, the Saint Louis brewer behind Budweiser, was American for well over a century. Then came two thousand eight.

lines.text: In July 2008, InBev agreed to buy it for $70 a share in cash, about $52 billion.
lines.say: In July two thousand eight, InBev agreed to buy it for seventy dollars a share in cash, about fifty-two billion dollars.

lines.text: The new company was called Anheuser-Busch InBev, or AB InBev. And it wasn't done shopping.
lines.say: The new company was called Anheuser-Busch InBev, or A B InBev. And it wasn't done shopping.

lines.text: In 2016 it closed its biggest deal yet: SABMiller, then the world's number two brewer, with strong sales in Africa and Latin America.
lines.say: In twenty sixteen it closed its biggest deal yet: SABMiller, then the world's number two brewer, with strong sales in Africa and Latin America.

lines.text: The final offer was 45 pounds a share, which valued SABMiller at about 79 billion pounds.
lines.say: The final offer was forty-five pounds a share, which valued SABMiller at about seventy-nine billion pounds.

lines.text: Most of it was paid with borrowed money, and that debt shaped almost every big choice since.
lines.say: Most of it was paid with borrowed money, and that debt shaped almost every big choice since.

lines.text: Net debt went from $42.2 billion at the end of 2015 to $108 billion a year later.
lines.say: Net debt went from forty-two point two billion dollars at the end of twenty fifteen to one hundred eight billion dollars a year later.

lines.text: What did all those deals buy? A portfolio of more than 500 brands, sold in nearly every corner of the planet.
lines.say: What did all those deals buy? A portfolio of more than five hundred brands, sold in nearly every corner of the planet.

lines.text: Some you know: Budweiser, Corona, Stella Artois and Michelob Ultra. The company says it has 20 billion-dollar beer brands.
lines.say: Some you know: Budweiser, Corona, Stella Artois and Michelob Ultra. The company says it has twenty billion-dollar beer brands.

lines.text: And by its count for 2025, Corona and Budweiser are the two most valuable beer brands in the world.
lines.say: And by its count for twenty twenty-five, Corona and Budweiser are the two most valuable beer brands in the world.

lines.text: Big brands matter because a brewer's real product isn't beer. It's a name people will pay a little extra for.
lines.say: Big brands matter because a brewer's real product isn't beer. It's a name people will pay a little extra for.

lines.text: Chapter 2: How a brewer earns
lines.say: Chapter two: how a brewer earns.

lines.text: Brewers measure everything in hectoliters. One hectoliter is 100 liters, about 282 twelve-ounce cans.
lines.say: Brewers measure everything in hectoliters. One hectoliter is one hundred liters, about two hundred eighty-two twelve-ounce cans.

lines.text: In 2025, AB InBev sold 561.1 million hectoliters of beer and other drinks.
lines.say: In twenty twenty-five, A B InBev sold five hundred sixty-one point one million hectoliters of beer and other drinks.

lines.text: That's where our 158 billion cans comes from. Our math: 56.1 billion liters, divided by about a third of a liter per can.
lines.say: That's where our one hundred fifty-eight billion cans comes from. Our math: fifty-six point one billion liters, divided by about a third of a liter per can.

lines.text: Now the money. Our math: $59.3 billion of revenue divided by 561.1 million hectoliters is about $106 per hectoliter.
lines.say: Now the money. Our math: fifty-nine point three billion dollars of revenue divided by five hundred sixty-one point one million hectoliters is about one hundred six dollars per hectoliter.

lines.text: Shrink that to one 12-ounce can, and AB InBev takes in about 38 cents.
lines.say: Shrink that to one twelve-ounce can, and A B InBev takes in about thirty-eight cents.

lines.text: That's an average across every single country, brand and pack size it sells.
lines.say: That's an average across every single country, brand and pack size it sells.

lines.text: And it's revenue after excise taxes, so the shelf price you see is much higher.
lines.say: And it's revenue after excise taxes, so the shelf price you see is much higher.

lines.text: The rest of what you pay goes to taxes, the distributor that trucks it, and the store or bar that sells it.
lines.say: The rest of what you pay goes to taxes, the distributor that trucks it, and the store or bar that sells it.

lines.text: Out of that 38 cents comes the cost of making it: barley and malt, water, hops, aluminum cans, glass bottles and trucks.
lines.say: Out of that thirty-eight cents comes the cost of making it: barley and malt, water, hops, aluminum cans, glass bottles and trucks.

lines.text: Packaging is a big piece of that bill, and the brewer fills billions of cans, which is why metal prices matter so much.
lines.say: Packaging is a big piece of that bill, and the brewer fills billions of cans, which is why metal prices matter so much.

lines.text: After those costs and the company's overhead, what's left is normalized EBITDA: profit before interest, taxes and wear on the breweries.
lines.say: After those costs and the company's overhead, what's left is normalized E B I T D A: profit before interest, taxes and wear on the breweries.

lines.text: In 2025 it was $21.2 billion, on that $59.3 billion of revenue.
lines.say: In twenty twenty-five it was twenty-one point two billion dollars, on that fifty-nine point three billion dollars of revenue.

lines.text: That's a 35.8% margin, very high for something you can buy at any gas station.
lines.say: That's a thirty-five point eight percent margin, very high for something you can buy at any gas station.

lines.text: Per can, our math says about 13 cents of that 38 cents is left as EBITDA. That's roughly one third.
lines.say: Per can, our math says about thirteen cents of that thirty-eight cents is left as E B I T D A. That's roughly one third.

lines.text: Thirteen cents sounds small, until you multiply it by 158 billion cans a year.
lines.say: Thirteen cents sounds small, until you multiply it by one hundred fifty-eight billion cans a year.

lines.text: So how did it earn more while selling less? Revenue per hectoliter rose 4.4% in 2025.
lines.say: So how did it earn more while selling less? Revenue per hectoliter rose four point four percent in twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: The company credits two things: smarter pricing, and nudging drinkers toward pricier premium brands.
lines.say: The company credits two things: smarter pricing, and nudging drinkers toward pricier premium brands.

lines.text: Those premium, above-core brands made up 35% of revenue in 2025. Same can, fancier label, bigger price.
lines.say: Those premium, above-core brands made up thirty-five percent of revenue in twenty twenty-five. Same can, fancier label, bigger price.

lines.text: Scale helps too. One giant buyer of barley and cans gets better deals than a small brewer ever could.
lines.say: Scale helps too. One giant buyer of barley and cans gets better deals than a small brewer ever could.

lines.text: Chapter 3: Where the profit is
lines.say: Chapter three: where the profit is.

lines.text: Here's something most Americans never guess. The biggest profit pools aren't in the United States.
lines.say: Here's something most Americans never guess. The biggest profit pools aren't in the United States.

lines.text: AB InBev splits the world into five regions: North America, Middle Americas, South America, EMEA, and Asia Pacific.
lines.say: A B InBev splits the world into five regions: North America, Middle Americas, South America, E M E A, and Asia Pacific.

lines.text: Take the fourth quarter of 2025. Middle Americas, led by Mexico and Colombia, earned $2.5 billion of EBITDA on $4.9 billion of revenue.
lines.say: Take the fourth quarter of twenty twenty-five. Middle Americas, led by Mexico and Colombia, earned two point five billion dollars of E B I T D A on four point nine billion dollars of revenue.

lines.text: By our math, that's a margin of about 51%. More than half of every dollar left over before those big costs.
lines.say: By our math, that's a margin of about fifty-one percent. More than half of every dollar left over before those big costs.

lines.text: North America earned $906 million on $3.2 billion of revenue. Our math puts that margin near 28%.
lines.say: North America earned nine hundred six million dollars on three point two billion dollars of revenue. Our math puts that margin near twenty-eight percent.

lines.text: Why the gap? In Mexico it's the biggest brewer by a wide margin, and that kind of scale pays.
lines.say: Why the gap? In Mexico it's the biggest brewer by a wide margin, and that kind of scale pays.

lines.text: South America, mostly Brazil, earned $1.3 billion on $3.6 billion in the same quarter. That's about 36%, by our math.
lines.say: South America, mostly Brazil, earned one point three billion dollars on three point six billion dollars in the same quarter. That's about thirty-six percent, by our math.

lines.text: In Brazil, revenue per hectoliter rose 5.4% in 2025. Same story: more money per drink.
lines.say: In Brazil, revenue per hectoliter rose five point four percent in twenty twenty-five. Same story: more money per drink.

lines.text: Corona is the star export. In 2025 its revenue outside Mexico grew 8.3%, with double-digit volume growth in 30 markets.
lines.say: Corona is the star export. In twenty twenty-five its revenue outside Mexico grew eight point three percent, with double-digit volume growth in thirty markets.

lines.text: One catch: in the United States, Corona isn't theirs to sell. Constellation Brands has owned those US rights since 2013.
lines.say: One catch: in the United States, Corona isn't theirs to sell. Constellation Brands has owned those US rights since twenty thirteen.

lines.text: Chapter 4: The $108 billion hangover
lines.say: Chapter four: the one hundred eight billion dollar hangover.

lines.text: Investors watch one number to judge that debt: net debt divided by EBITDA. It's how many years of profit it would take to pay it off.
lines.say: Investors watch one number to judge that debt: net debt divided by E B I T D A. It's how many years of profit it would take to pay it off.

lines.text: Here it is at the end of every year from 2015 to 2025. Before SABMiller, it was about 2.5 times. After the deal closed, it jumped to 5.5 times.
lines.say: Here it is at the end of every year from twenty fifteen to twenty twenty-five. Before SABMiller, it was about two point five times. After the deal closed, it jumped to five point five times.

lines.text: At 5.5 times, it would take five and a half years of all its EBITDA just to clear the slate.
lines.say: At five point five times, it would take five and a half years of all its E B I T D A just to clear the slate.

lines.text: It worked down to about 4 times by 2019, counting a pending sale. Then 2020 hit, bars closed, profit fell, and the ratio bounced back to about 4.8.
lines.say: It worked down to about four times by twenty nineteen, counting a pending sale. Then twenty twenty hit, bars closed, profit fell, and the ratio bounced back to about four point eight.

lines.text: To pay down debt, it sold things. In 2020, it sold a 49.9% stake in its US can plants for about $3 billion.
lines.say: To pay down debt, it sold things. In twenty twenty, it sold a forty-nine point nine percent stake in its US can plants for about three billion dollars.

lines.text: In 2018 it also cut its dividend in half, sending more cash to lenders instead of shareholders.
lines.say: In twenty eighteen it also cut its dividend in half, sending more cash to lenders instead of shareholders.

lines.text: Slowly it worked. By the end of 2024, the ratio was about 2.9 times, its first time under 3 since 2015.
lines.say: Slowly it worked. By the end of twenty twenty-four, the ratio was about two point nine times, its first time under three since twenty fifteen.

lines.text: And at the end of 2025 it was still about 2.9 times, on about $61 billion of net debt.
lines.say: And at the end of twenty twenty-five it was still about two point nine times, on about sixty-one billion dollars of net debt.

lines.text: With debt under control, the cash is flowing the other way. Free cash flow was $11.3 billion in 2025.
lines.say: With debt under control, the cash is flowing the other way. Free cash flow was eleven point three billion dollars in twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: In October 2025 it announced a $6 billion share buyback, and its dividends for 2025 add up to 1.15 euros a share.
lines.say: In October twenty twenty-five it announced a six billion dollar share buyback, and its dividends for twenty twenty-five add up to one point one five euros a share.

lines.text: And in January 2026, it bought back that can-plant stake, for about the same $3 billion it sold it for.
lines.say: And in January twenty twenty-six, it bought back that can-plant stake, for about the same three billion dollars it sold it for.

lines.text: Owning the plants again gives it more control over its own cans, just as aluminum got more expensive in America.
lines.say: Owning the plants again gives it more control over its own cans, just as aluminum got more expensive in America.

lines.text: Chapter 5: Shocks and new bets
lines.say: Chapter five: shocks and new bets.

lines.text: The biggest recent shock came in 2023. A Bud Light social media promotion in April set off a consumer boycott.
lines.say: The biggest recent shock came in twenty twenty-three. A Bud Light social media promotion in April set off a consumer boycott.

lines.text: We'll stick to the business numbers. In May 2023, Bud Light lost its spot as America's best-selling beer to Modelo Especial.
lines.say: We'll stick to the business numbers. In May twenty twenty-three, Bud Light lost its spot as America's best-selling beer to Modelo Especial.

lines.text: Modelo is sold in the US by Constellation Brands, a different company. So those sales went to a rival.
lines.say: Modelo is sold in the US by Constellation Brands, a different company. So those sales went to a rival.

lines.text: For all of 2023, Anheuser-Busch's US revenue fell 9.5%, and its sales to retailers dropped 11.9%.
lines.say: For all of twenty twenty-three, Anheuser-Busch's US revenue fell nine point five percent, and its sales to retailers dropped eleven point nine percent.

lines.text: In the second quarter of 2023 alone, its US EBITDA fell 28.2%.
lines.say: In the second quarter of twenty twenty-three alone, its US E B I T D A fell twenty-eight point two percent.

lines.text: But here's the global view. That same year, AB InBev's total revenue still rose 7.8% to $59.4 billion, a record at the time.
lines.say: But here's the global view. That same year, A B InBev's total revenue still rose seven point eight percent to fifty-nine point four billion dollars, a record at the time.

lines.text: That's the upside of owning beer in dozens of countries. One market can stumble while Mexico and Brazil keep pouring.
lines.say: That's the upside of owning beer in dozens of countries. One market can stumble while Mexico and Brazil keep pouring.

lines.text: Then a twist. In September 2025, data firm Circana ranked Michelob Ultra the top-selling US beer by volume, passing Modelo.
lines.say: Then a twist. In September twenty twenty-five, data firm Circana ranked Michelob Ultra the top-selling US beer by volume, passing Modelo.

lines.text: Modelo still led in dollar sales, but the number one spot by volume was back in Anheuser-Busch's hands.
lines.say: Modelo still led in dollar sales, but the number one spot by volume was back in Anheuser-Busch's hands.

lines.text: Another pressure is the cost of the can itself.
lines.say: Another pressure is the cost of the can itself.

lines.text: The US doubled its tariff on imported aluminum to 50% in June 2025.
lines.say: The US doubled its tariff on imported aluminum to fifty percent in June twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: And there's a slow shift in drinking itself. Volume fell 2.3% in 2025, and beer alone fell 2.6%.
lines.say: And there's a slow shift in drinking itself. Volume fell two point three percent in twenty twenty-five, and beer alone fell two point six percent.

lines.text: So the company is betting on drinks without the alcohol in them.
lines.say: So the company is betting on drinks without the alcohol in them.

lines.text: Its no-alcohol beer revenue grew 34% in 2025.
lines.say: Its no-alcohol beer revenue grew thirty-four percent in twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: Corona Cero leads that push worldwide, and in the US, Michelob Ultra Zero was a top new beer of 2025.
lines.say: Corona Cero leads that push worldwide, and in the US, Michelob Ultra Zero was a top new beer of twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: It's also pushing what it calls Beyond Beer, like canned cocktails and seltzers. That's about 3% of revenue so far.
lines.say: It's also pushing what it calls Beyond Beer, like canned cocktails and seltzers. That's about three percent of revenue so far.

lines.text: If people drink less beer, it can sell them something else in the same can, through the same trucks.
lines.say: If people drink less beer, it can sell them something else in the same can, through the same trucks.

lines.text: Whether that works is an open question, and we won't guess.

lines.text: Chapter 6: The recap
lines.say: Chapter six: the recap.

lines.text: AB InBev was built by buying other brewers, first Anheuser-Busch in 2008, then SABMiller in 2016.
lines.say: A B InBev was built by buying other brewers, first Anheuser-Busch in two thousand eight, then SABMiller in twenty sixteen.

lines.text: In 2025, it took in about 38 cents per can-sized drink, and kept about 13 cents as EBITDA, by our math.
lines.say: In twenty twenty-five, it took in about thirty-eight cents per can-sized drink, and kept about thirteen cents as E B I T D A, by our math.

lines.text: It grows by charging more per hectoliter and selling premium brands, even while total volume slips.
lines.say: It grows by charging more per hectoliter and selling premium brands, even while total volume slips.

lines.text: And the debt from SABMiller went from about 5.5 times EBITDA in 2016 to about 2.9 times in 2025.
lines.say: And the debt from SABMiller went from about five point five times E B I T D A in twenty sixteen to about two point nine times in twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: Its richest profits come from Mexico, Colombia and Brazil, where it's the biggest brewer by far.
lines.say: Its richest profits come from Mexico, Colombia and Brazil, where it's the biggest brewer by far.

lines.text: And for you, the drinker? A good chunk of what you pay for a premium label is the label. Now you know the math.

post.title: How Anheuser-Busch Makes Money: 38 Cents a Can, 158 Billion Cans' Worth a Year
post.ig: The world's biggest brewer takes in about 38 cents per can, by our math for 2025. Here's where it all goes.
post.tiktok: AB InBev sold less beer in 2025 and still earned more. Here's the per-can math.
post.yt_desc:
AB InBev, the owner of Anheuser-Busch, brought in $59.3 billion of revenue in 2025 and $21.2 billion of normalized EBITDA, a 35.8% margin, even though it sold 2.3% less volume. This video explains how the world's biggest brewer makes money: the 2008 and 2016 deals that built it, our per-can math (about 38 cents of revenue and 13 cents of EBITDA per 12-ounce can), where the richest profits are, and how it paid down the debt from SABMiller, charted from 2015 to 2025. We also cover the 2023 Bud Light sales drop, aluminum costs and the push into no-alcohol beer.

CHAPTERS

Per-can and per-hectoliter figures are our math from reported 2025 revenue, EBITDA and volume, averaged across all countries, brands and pack sizes. EBITDA is earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, not net profit.

Sources: AB InBev full-year results 2015 to 2025 (latest Feb 12, 2026, via SEC 6-K and Business Wire); AB InBev second-quarter 2023 results (Aug 2023); AB InBev 2023 annual report; BeverageDaily (Oct 2016); PBS NewsHour (July 14, 2008); ABC News (June 2023); Brewbound (Feb 2024); ABC News and Fox Business citing Circana (Sept 2025); Bloomberg and Food Dive (Jan 6, 2026); The Drinks Business (Jan 2026).

News and education, not financial advice.
